---
title: "Client-Side Source Code Analysis for Secrets and Keys"
sidebarTitle: "Source Code Analysis"
description: "Menu option 8 streams HTML, JS, JSON, and source maps (2 MB cap) then applies 15 severity-weighted patterns to detect credentials, API keys, and secrets."
---

The Source Code Analysis module (menu option **8**) scans client-side source code of the target application for secrets, credentials, and sensitive data that should never be publicly accessible. It downloads every reachable HTML page and linked asset — JavaScript bundles, JSON configs, source maps, CSS, YAML, XML, and `.env` files — then applies 15 regex pattern catalogues weighted by severity. Critical and high findings are automatically promoted to the global `FINDINGS` list with a `[CODE:SEV]` prefix so they appear in every report format.

## URL Sources

The module attempts to reuse previously discovered URLs in priority order:

<Steps>
  <Step title="Reuse Spider URLs">
    If the Spidering module (option 7) has already run in the current session, its discovered URLs are used as the seed list. This can provide hundreds of application pages to analyse without any additional HTTP requests.

    ```text
    [INFO] Usando 312 URLs del último spider.
    ```
  </Step>
  <Step title="Offer Quick Spider">
    If no spider data is available, the scanner offers to run a quick spider capped at 50 pages and depth 2 before proceeding:

    ```text
    [?] No hay spider previo. ¿Ejecutar spider rápido (max 50 páginas)? [S/n]:
    ```
  </Step>
  <Step title="Analyse Target Only">
    If the quick spider is declined, only the target URL is analysed. This is fast but misses secrets hidden in secondary pages or JavaScript bundles linked from deeper pages.
  </Step>
</Steps>

## File Download Logic

For each URL, `_download_text_capped` fetches the resource using `stream=True` to avoid loading large files into memory all at once:

- **2 MB cap per file** — any file whose `Content-Length` header exceeds 2 MB is skipped entirely. Files without a declared size are streamed and truncated at the 2 MB boundary.
- Assets are collected from `<script src>`, `<link href>`, and inline `sourceMappingURL` references found in HTML pages.
- Only assets on the **same domain** (`netloc`) as the target are downloaded.

### Asset Types Downloaded

| Extension / Content-Type | Examples |
|---|---|
| `.js`, `.mjs`, `.jsx`, `.ts`, `.tsx` | JavaScript bundles, React/Vue components |
| `.json` | API responses, config files |
| `.map` | Source maps (may contain original unminified source) |
| `.css` | Stylesheets (sometimes contain inline secrets or comments) |
| `.yml`, `.yaml` | Docker Compose, CI/CD configs |
| `.xml` | SOAP definitions, sitemap, Spring configs |
| `.env` | Environment variable files |
| `text/*`, `application/json`, `application/javascript` | Any text-based Content-Type |

## Pattern Catalogue (15 Patterns)

Patterns are applied in order of descending severity. Each match captures a ±30 character context window around the finding (then capped at 140 characters total) for the report snippet.

### Critical

<Accordion title="Private PEM Keys">
  Matches the header line of any PEM-encoded private key — RSA, EC, DSA, OpenSSH, and PGP formats:

  ```
  -----BEGIN (RSA |EC |DSA |OPENSSH |PGP )?PRIVATE KEY-----
  ```

  **Finding type:** `Clave privada PEM`
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Database Connection Strings with Embedded Credentials">
  Matches connection URIs for MongoDB, MySQL, PostgreSQL, Redis, AMQP, MSSQL, and JDBC formats where a `username:password@host` pair is embedded in the URL:

  ```
  \b(mongodb(\+srv)?|mysql|postgres(ql)?|redis|amqps?|mssql|jdbc:[a-z]+)://[^\s"'<>]*:[^\s"'<>@]+@[^\s"'<>]+
  ```

  **Finding type:** `Cadena de conexión BD con credenciales`
</Accordion>

### High

<Accordion title="AWS Access Key ID">
  Fixed-length 20-character strings starting with `AKIA` or `ASIA`:

  ```
  \b(AKIA|ASIA)[0-9A-Z]{16}\b
  ```
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="AWS Secret Access Key">
  Contextual match: variable name containing `aws_secret` or `aws_sk` followed by a 40-character base64 string.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Google API Key">
  `AIza` prefix followed by 35 alphanumeric characters:

  ```
  \bAIza[0-9A-Za-z\-_]{35}\b
  ```
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="GitHub Tokens">
  Classic and fine-grained personal access tokens, OAuth app tokens, and GitHub App installation tokens:

  ```
  \bgh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9]{30,}\b
  ```
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Slack Tokens">
  Bot, app, legacy, and workspace tokens matching the `xox*-` prefix pattern:

  ```
  \bxox[abpros]-[A-Za-z0-9\-]{10,}\b
  ```
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Stripe Live Secret Keys">
  Production secret keys starting with `sk_live_`:

  ```
  \bsk_live_[0-9a-zA-Z]{20,}\b
  ```
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="JWT Tokens">
  Three base64url-encoded segments separated by dots, matching the `eyJ` header prefix of standard JWTs:

  ```
  \beyJ[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{8,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{8,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{4,}\b
  ```
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Hardcoded Credentials (Generic)">
  Captures the value from common credential variable names. Matches assignment syntax in JavaScript, Python, PHP, JSON, YAML, and similar formats:

  ```
  (?i)(?:password|passwd|pwd|secret|api[_-]?key|access[_-]?key|
  client[_-]?secret|auth[_-]?token|bearer)["'\s:=]{1,8}["']([^"'\s]{4,80})["']
  ```

  **Finding type:** `Credencial hardcoded`
</Accordion>

### Medium

<Accordion title="Sensitive HTML Comments">
  HTML comments containing security-relevant keywords: `password`, `api_key`, `private_key`, `bearer`, `backdoor`, `deprecated`, `do not commit`, `TODO`, `FIXME`, `XXX`, `HACK`, `backup file/path/server/db`, `internal use/api/server/tool`, and `debug enabled/mode/key/token`.

  ```html
  <!-- TODO: remove hardcoded password before deploy -->
  <!-- FIXME: admin bypass still active on staging -->
  ```

  Pure UI/layout comments (footer, navbar, logo, carousel, etc.) that contain no credential keywords are filtered out automatically.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Basic Auth in URLs">
  HTTP/HTTPS URLs with embedded `user:password@` credentials:

  ```
  \bhttps?://[A-Za-z0-9._\-]+:[^\s"'<>@/]+@[A-Za-z0-9._\-]+
  ```
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Exposed Source Maps">
  `sourceMappingURL` comments in JavaScript that reference an external `.map` file — these can expose the full original unminified source code:

  ```
  //# sourceMappingURL=app.bundle.js.map
  ```
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Private IP Addresses (Hardcoded)">
  RFC 1918 private address ranges hardcoded in client-side code:
  - `10.0.0.0/8`
  - `192.168.0.0/16`
  - `172.16.0.0/12`
</Accordion>

### Low

<Accordion title="Sensitive Internal Paths">
  String literals referencing known sensitive paths that should not appear in client-side code:

  ```
  "/admin", "/adminer", "/debug", "/console", "/h2-console",
  "/phpmyadmin", "/backup", "/backups", "/dump", "/wp-admin",
  "/actuator", "/internal", "/staging", "/.git", "/.env"
  ```
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Exposed Email Addresses">
  Standard email regex for addresses embedded in source code that may reveal internal usernames, support addresses, or infrastructure owners.
</Accordion>

## Deduplication

All findings across all downloaded pages and assets are globally deduplicated by the composite key:

```python
(type, value[:80].lower(), url)
```

This prevents the same hardcoded password from being reported dozens of times if it appears in a minified bundle referenced from every page on the site.

## Findings Promotion to FINDINGS

Only **critical** and **high** severity findings are promoted to the global `FINDINGS` list with a `[CODE:SEV]` prefix:

```text
[CODE:CRITICAL] Clave privada PEM en https://example.com/js/app.bundle.js — valor: -----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----
[CODE:HIGH]     AWS Access Key ID en https://example.com/config.js — valor: AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE
[CODE:HIGH]     Credencial hardcoded en https://example.com/api.js — valor: supersecret123
```

Medium, low, and informational findings appear in the detailed per-severity tables in terminal output and in all report formats, but do not inflate the primary `FINDINGS` count.

## Data Stored in SCAN_DATA

```json title="SCAN_DATA['source_code_analysis'] structure"
{
  "pages_analyzed": 120,
  "assets_analyzed": 47,
  "total_findings": 23,
  "summary": {
    "critical": 1,
    "high": 3,
    "medium": 8,
    "low": 11
  },
  "findings": [
    {
      "severity": "critical",
      "type": "Clave privada PEM",
      "value": "-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----",
      "url": "https://example.com/js/keys.js",
      "snippet": "...exports.key = '-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----\\n..."
    },
    {
      "severity": "high",
      "type": "AWS Access Key ID",
      "value": "AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE",
      "url": "https://example.com/config.js",
      "snippet": "...AWS_KEY = 'AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE'; /..."
    }
  ]
}
```

<Warning>
  Source maps (`.map` files) can expose the complete original source code of your application to anyone who requests them. If the scanner finds an exposed source map, treat it as a high-priority remediation item regardless of whether any secrets are found within it.
</Warning>

<Tip>
  Run the Spider module (option 7) before Source Code Analysis. The spider's discovered URLs are used directly as the download seed list — a 300-URL spider result means 300 pages plus all their linked assets are scanned for secrets, versus just the single landing page without it.
</Tip>
